bugs.name: Wiki Bold toolbar formatting renders as regular text in preview and saved pages
bugs.summary: The Wiki editor’s Bold toolbar inserts Markdown markers, but the sample renders in regular weight in both Preview and the saved page.
bugs.expected: Selecting text and using the Bold toolbar control should render that text visibly bold in Preview and on the saved Wiki page.
bugs.actual: The editor inserted `**Tablet formatting sample**`, but Preview and the saved page both displayed “Tablet formatting sample” in regular weight. The Markdown markers were not visible in the rendered page.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open the repository Wiki. Create a disposable page and enter Tablet formatting sample.
Select the text and click the Bold toolbar control. Confirm the editor wraps the selection in ** markers.
Open Preview and inspect the apparent font weight, then save the page through Save Page and inspect its rendered text.
bugs.reason: The user rejected the reported weak Wiki bold after reviewing the evidence. Both Preview and the saved page contain the expected strong markup, with semibold weight 600 versus paragraph weight 400. A separate saved-page browser confirmed that rendering, and a clean browser font control reproduced weak emphasis without Gitea assets. This supports a font-environment explanation rather than a Wiki formatting failure, while the exact font used by the original Mo browser remains unproven. The rejection does not rest on markup alone or on a confirmed universal font root cause.

bugs.name: Markdown Wiki links open the Pages index instead of their target
bugs.summary: Clicking a rendered Markdown link to a freshly saved Wiki page repeatedly opens the Pages index instead of the linked page.
bugs.expected: Clicking the rendered link on NAV-Q8R-Guide opens the existing NAV-Q8R-Target Wiki page.
bugs.actual: Following the agent-authored absolute Markdown URL ending /wiki/NAV-Q8R-Target opened the Pages index. The actual saved page URL and Gitea-generated link end /wiki/NAV-Q8R-Target.-; following that generated link opens the target successfully.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open the seeded eval/harbor-handbook Wiki.
Create a disposable page titled NAV-Q8R-Target with a short body and observe the generated URL ending NAV-Q8R-Target.-.
Create NAV-Q8R-Guide with an absolute Markdown link to the same fixture origin and repository, but manually end its path with /wiki/NAV-Q8R-Target, omitting the .- marker.
Follow that rendered body link; it opens the Pages index because it does not address the literal-hyphen title.
From the Pages index, follow the application-generated NAV-Q8R-Target link, whose path ends .-. Confirm the target and its saved body open successfully.
bugs.reason: User-approved rejection: the agent supplied the wrong absolute URL. Gitea uses hyphens for spaces unless the .- marker preserves literal hyphens. The report’s claimed suffix-free saved target URL is contradicted by its native trace. Markdown preserves the supplied URL; the canonical generated target link works.

bugs.name: Wiki clone menu shows the main repository's Tea CLI clone command
bugs.summary: The report says that on a wiki page, the Code menu's Tea CLI tab shows the main repository's clone command instead of the wiki's.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the wiki's Tea CLI clone command targets the wiki.
bugs.actual: On a wiki page, selecting Tea CLI in the Code menu was reported to show 'tea clone eval/harbor-handbook', the main repository's command.
reproSteps: Open a repository wiki page.
Open the Code menu and choose Tea CLI.
Read the full clone command in the field.
bugs.reason: The wiki's Tea CLI command is correct: it is 'tea clone <owner>/<repo>.wiki', and the HTTPS URL also ends in .wiki.git. The read-only field is only about 30 characters wide, so the command is cut off on screen right before '.wiki'; the full value (and what the copy button copies) includes it. The report read only the visible part. The main repository's menu correctly shows the command without '.wiki'.

bugs.name: Relative Markdown link to a hyphenated wiki page opens the Pages index
bugs.summary: The report says that a relative Markdown link such as [Start navigation](NAV-Start) on a wiki page opens the wiki's Pages index instead of the saved page NAV-Start.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the link opens the NAV-Start page.
bugs.actual: Clicking [Start navigation](NAV-Start) on Home opened the Pages index; the NAV-Start row there opened the page at /wiki/NAV-Start.-.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page titled with a hyphen, such as NAV-Start.
On another wiki page, add the Markdown link [Start navigation](NAV-Start) and save.
Click the link.
bugs.reason: Intended: in wiki paths Gitea treats '-' as a space and marks a literal hyphen with the '.-' suffix, so a page titled NAV-Start is saved at NAV-Start.- and a link to plain NAV-Start names a page called 'NAV Start', which doesn't exist; a missing page opens the Pages index. A link to NAV-Start.-, or one generated by Gitea, opens the page. This is the same path scheme as the existing rejection 'Markdown Wiki links open the Pages index instead of their target', here with a relative link instead of an absolute URL.

bugs.name: Root-relative Markdown image displays broken image in legacy side-by-side preview
bugs.summary: The report says that a root-relative image (/avatars/…) shows as a broken image in the wiki's side-by-side preview.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that an image path starting with / loads from the site root, as it would on the Gitea site itself.
bugs.actual: An image written as /avatars/<hash> in a wiki page showed as broken in the preview and on the saved page; the image URL pointed into the wiki's own files and returned 404.
reproSteps: Edit a wiki page and add a Markdown image whose path starts with /, such as /avatars/<hash>.
Open the side-by-side preview, then save and view the page.
Check whether the image loads and where its URL points.
bugs.reason: Intended: a wiki image path starting with / (for example /avatars/<hash>) resolves to the wiki's own files (/<owner>/<repo>/wiki/raw/avatars/<hash>), not the site root, so it 404s. This is the same in every preview and on the saved page. Since 1.23 (go-gitea/gitea#34114), leading-slash paths are relative to the current content, so content stays portable when it's cloned, mirrored or served under a sub-path; /:root/... links to the site root, and a unit test asserts /image resolves to wiki/raw/image (models/renderhelper/repo_wiki_test.go:48). Same rule as the known-invalid 'Root-relative links in issue Markdown are prefixed with the repository path'.

bugs.name: Wiki page titled '.' is saved as 'unnamed'
bugs.summary: The report says that a wiki page saved with the title "." ends up named "unnamed".
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the page keeps the title ".".
bugs.actual: Saving a page titled "." created /wiki/unnamed with the content kept.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with the title "." and some content, and save.
Check the resulting page's name and URL.
bugs.reason: Intended: "." isn't a usable file name in the wiki repository, so Gitea deliberately maps it to "unnamed", and an upstream unit test asserts that. The missing notice about the rename is a separate accepted entry; this entry covers only the claim that the title itself should have been kept.

bugs.name: Exiting an automatic list leaves following text in the last item
bugs.summary: Pressing Enter twice after a bullet removes the automatic bullet but does not create the blank line needed to end the Markdown list. The following unbulleted text joins the previous item in Preview.
bugs.expected: After exiting the automatic list, Tail paragraph should render as a separate paragraph outside the list.
bugs.actual: Preview shows two bullets: First and Second Tail paragraph. Write mode contains - First, - Second and Tail paragraph on consecutive lines without a blank separator. A whole-page assertion confirmed Tail paragraph is not a separate paragraph.
reproSteps: In the wiki Markdown editor, type - First and press Enter.
Type Second, then press Enter twice and type Tail paragraph.
Open Preview and observe Tail paragraph continuing the final list item without a separating blank line.
bugs.reason: User rejected this as normal Markdown behavior: unbulleted text immediately after a list item, without a blank separator, can continue that item. The reported Write-mode source and Preview are consistent. This rejection does not establish that every automatic-list editing interaction is correct.

bugs.name: _Sidebar content missing on wiki pages that have headings (TOC replaces sidebar)
bugs.summary: The report says that once a wiki page has headings, so a Table of Contents is generated, the custom _Sidebar content (for example 'Sidebar Home') is no longer shown and only the Table of Contents appears in .wiki-content-sidebar.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the sidebar shows both the Table of Contents and the _Sidebar content with its edit pencil.
bugs.actual: On pages with one or more headings, the sidebar showed the Table of Contents and, below it, the _Sidebar content with its edit pencil, after reloads and at narrow widths too.
reproSteps: Create a _Sidebar wiki page with some content.
Create a wiki page with no headings and check the sidebar.
Edit the page to add a heading, save, and check the sidebar again.
bugs.reason: Not reproducible: the wiki page renders the Table of Contents and the _Sidebar content as two separate blocks that both use the wiki-content-sidebar class, and adding a heading only adds the Table of Contents block above the _Sidebar block. A check that reads just the first .wiki-content-sidebar element sees only the Table of Contents, which most likely explains the report.

bugs.name: Clicking an in-page wiki heading link doesn't scroll to the heading
bugs.summary: The report claims that clicking a Markdown link such as [Go](#heading) or a heading's anchor icon on a wiki page does not scroll to that heading.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the click to scroll the heading into view.
bugs.actual: The reporter says the view stays in place after the click.
reproSteps: Create a long wiki page with a link [Go Unicode](#日本語-café--punctuation) and the heading '## 日本語 café & punctuation!' far below it.
Click Go Unicode.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: clicking an in-page link scrolls to the heading, including Unicode headings, because anchors.ts handles link clicks and adds the 'user-content-' id prefix. Only same-tab fragment changes that are not clicks fail to scroll, which is the accepted gitea-wiki-fragment-change-does-not-scroll.

bugs.name: Opening or reloading a wiki URL with a heading fragment doesn't scroll to the heading
bugs.summary: The report claims that opening a wiki page URL that ends in a heading fragment, or reloading it, does not scroll to that heading, for example for a Unicode heading.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the page to load scrolled to the heading.
bugs.actual: The reporter says the page loads at the top or at a different heading.
reproSteps: Create a long wiki page with the heading '## 日本語 café & punctuation!' far down.
Open the page URL with #%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E8%AA%9E-caf%C3%A9--punctuation appended in a new tab, or reload it.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: on page load anchors.ts decodes the fragment and scrolls to the prefixed heading id, so a fresh load at an ASCII or Unicode fragment lands on the heading. A reload may restore the browser's previous scroll position, which is browser behavior. Only same-tab fragment changes that are not clicks fail to scroll, which is the accepted gitea-wiki-fragment-change-does-not-scroll.

bugs.name: Undo leaves bold markers applied with Ctrl+B in the simple Markdown editor
bugs.summary: The report claims that in the default (simple textarea) Markdown editor, Ctrl+B wraps the selection in ** markers and Ctrl+Z then leaves those markers in place.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects Ctrl+Z to remove the bold markers Ctrl+B added.
bugs.actual: After applying bold with the toolbar, toggling it off with the toolbar, then pressing Ctrl+B and Ctrl+Z, the text read 'Harbor **middle** tail'.
reproSteps: In a wiki page editor using the simple textarea editor, enter 'Harbor middle tail' and select 'middle'.
Click the Bold toolbar button twice to apply and remove bold.
Press Ctrl+B, then Ctrl+Z, and read the text.
bugs.reason: Not a bug. The simple editor has no keyboard shortcuts: @github/markdown-toolbar-element 2.2.3 only handles Space/Enter on a focused toolbar button, Gitea's textarea keydown handler (web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts) only handles Tab and Enter, and the Bold tooltip ('Add bold text') advertises no shortcut. Ctrl+B therefore changes nothing; the ** markers reappear because Ctrl+Z correctly undoes the earlier toolbar toggle-off, and a second Ctrl+Z removes them. Undo after the Bold button works.

bugs.name: Root-relative Markdown link to the wiki opens the Pages list instead of Home
bugs.summary: The report claims that a wiki link written with a leading slash and the full repository path, such as [Home navigation](/owner/repo/wiki) in _Sidebar or a page, opens the wiki's Pages list instead of Home.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the link to open the wiki's Home page.
reproSteps: In a wiki with a Home page, save a page or _Sidebar containing [Home navigation](/<owner>/<repo>/wiki).
Click Home navigation.
bugs.reason: Intended: since Gitea 1.23 (go-gitea/gitea#34114) a link starting with / in wiki content resolves relative to the wiki (models/renderhelper/repo_wiki.go ResolveLink; repo_wiki_test.go asserts /test renders as /user2/repo1/wiki/test). The link therefore renders as /<owner>/<repo>/wiki/<owner>/<repo>/wiki, a page that doesn't exist, and a missing wiki page redirects to the Pages list (routers/web/repo/wiki.go). /Home, Home, [[Home]], a full URL and /:root/<owner>/<repo>/wiki all open Home. Same rule as the known-invalid root-relative wiki image entry.

bugs.name: Wiki Pages list shows the special _Sidebar and _Footer pages
bugs.summary: The report says the wiki Pages list (?action=_pages) lists _Sidebar and _Footer as ordinary pages, while the Page dropdown on wiki pages hides them.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the Pages list hides _Sidebar and _Footer, as the Page dropdown does.
bugs.actual: With pages Home, Guide, _Sidebar and _Footer, the Page dropdown listed only Guide and Home, while ?action=_pages listed _Footer, _Sidebar, Guide and Home. Opening _Sidebar from the list showed the page with Edit, history and Delete Page.
reproSteps: In a repository wiki, create pages Home, Guide, _Sidebar and _Footer.
Open a wiki page and expand the Page dropdown.
Open the Pages list (?action=_pages) and compare.
bugs.reason: Intended upstream behavior. Only the Page dropdown in renderViewPage skips _Sidebar and _Footer (routers/web/repo/wiki.go); WikiPages lists every wiki file, and it is the listing that opens those pages with their history and Delete actions. Upstream main is unchanged.

bugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor silently discards newer edits
bugs.summary: The wiki editor carries no record of the revision it was opened from, so saving an editor opened before another save replaces the page with the older body. The newer saved change disappears without warning, unlike Gitea's file editor and issue editor, which reject the same stale save.
bugs.expected: When the page changed after the editor was opened, the save is refused with a conflict message (as the repository file editor and issue description editor do) or the edits are merged, and the newer saved change is kept.
bugs.actual: Two editors are opened on a checklist page with 'Check ropes' and 'Check tide'. The second editor adds 'Check radio' and saves. The first, now stale, changes only 'Check ropes' to 'Check ropes carefully' and saves successfully with no warning. The page now lists 'Check ropes carefully' and 'Check tide'; 'Check radio' is gone, and the new revision's diff deletes it. Reload confirms the loss. The same happens across two users.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with a checklist containing 'Check ropes' and 'Check tide'.
Open that page's Edit form in two tabs before saving either.
In the second tab, append 'Check radio' and click Save Page.
In the first tab, change only 'Check ropes' to 'Check ropes carefully' and click Save Page.
Reload the page and observe 'Check radio' is gone, with no warning shown at save time.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: a stale multi-tab save that overwrites newer saved data is last-write-wins. Nothing on this screen says the save will leave the other fields alone, and conflict warnings elsewhere in Gitea are a nice-to-have here, not a promise.

bugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor after the page was deleted silently recreates it
bugs.summary: If a wiki page is deleted in one tab, saving an editor for that page that was opened earlier in another tab silently creates the page again, with no warning that it was deleted.
bugs.expected: Saving an editor for a wiki page that was deleted in the meantime warns that the page no longer exists instead of silently recreating it.
bugs.actual: After the page was deleted (and gone from the page list), saving the stale editor recreated the page with the editor's content and no deletion or conflict warning.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page and open its Edit form in tab A.
In tab B, delete the page and confirm.
In tab A, change the content and click Save Page.
Check whether the page exists again and whether any warning appeared.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: a stale multi-tab save that overwrites newer saved data is last-write-wins. Nothing on this screen says the save will leave the other fields alone, and conflict warnings elsewhere in Gitea are a nice-to-have here, not a promise.

bugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor after the page is renamed recreates the old page
bugs.summary: If a wiki page is renamed in one tab and an editor opened earlier in another tab then saves a body-only edit, Gitea silently creates a new page at the old title instead of warning or editing the renamed page, splitting the content across two pages.
bugs.expected: A stale edit to a page that was renamed elsewhere is rejected with a conflict warning or applied to the renamed page; it doesn't create a second page at the old title.
bugs.actual: The stale save succeeded with no warning and created a page at the old title holding the stale edit. The renamed page kept its earlier content, and the page list showed both titles.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page and open its editor in tab A without saving.
In tab B, edit the same page, change only its title, and save.
In tab A, change only the body and save.
Check the wiki page list and the contents of both titles.
bugs.reason: Works as intended: a stale multi-tab save that overwrites newer saved data is last-write-wins. Nothing on this screen says the save will leave the other fields alone, and conflict warnings elsewhere in Gitea are a nice-to-have here, not a promise.
